claims.text: Verified priorities: what the customer has said matters, with sources and dates. Stakeholder map: who decides, who informs, who owns metrics, and who controls dependencies. Systems and data landscape: known tools, likely content sources, and access constraints. Open questions: what you must learn, and from whom. Every customer fact should link to its source, not to a generated summary of it. Boundary Don't move restricted customer data into a partner workspace, and don't present a peer customer's story as this prospect's expected result. Use only authorized tools and sources.

claims.text: Positive Business Outcomes (PBOs) translate strategy into results a business owner would recognize. Metrics make them measurable. In preparation, both are hypotheses.
claims.checked_by: Studio author: drafted from the cited source text; no verbatim excerpt recorded; SME verification pending

claims.text: For each relevant line of business, draft one or two PBOs and three to five candidate metrics. Glean's Metrics Library groups metrics by function and warns against using the same metrics for every persona. A CIO cares about different measures than a sales director. For each metric, write down three things: What is measured: a precise definition, such as "mean handle time for password and access cases." How it will be measured: the system, the time window, and who supplies the data. Why it connects to the outcome: the logic linking the metric to the PBO.

claims.text: Choose a small, balanced set. A speed metric needs a quality guardrail, so that "faster" doesn't turn into "faster but worse." For support, a balanced set might pair handle time with resolution rate, escalation rate, and cost per resolved case. Mean handle time (agreed case class) | Efficiency | Captures effort per case First-contact resolution rate | Quality guardrail | Shows answers are still right Escalation rate to tier 2 | Quality and cost | Detects pushed-down complexity Cost per resolved case | Financial | Connects to the cost outcome Boundary These are hypotheses until the metric owner

claims.text: What: mean handle time for access-request tickets. How: compare consistent open-to-resolve timestamps in the IT service-management system over an agreed baseline period and a matching validation period. The service-desk manager supplies the export. Why: if agents find approved procedures faster, effort per ticket should fall and free capacity, provided first-contact resolution stays stable. Uncertainty: the definition of the ticket class and the data export must be confirmed by the metric owner.
